findings.message: strcpy() copies until the source terminator without a destination bound; it overflows whenever the source is longer than the destination.
gets() reads input with no destination bound.
sprintf() writes formatted output with no destination bound.
p is used (or freed again) after free() in the same function, with no reassignment in between.
This pointer comes from [malloc](1), which can return NULL, and is dereferenced without a check.
memcpy() size argument must be bounded by BOTH the destination capacity and the source length; verify it on every path (constant sizes overflow small or attacker-sized buffers too).

Hotspot #1 of 10 (score 6): 1 x variable-size copy/compare, 1 x write through variable index, 1 x read through variable index. Nearby checks were not taken as proof of safety -- real bugs are often a check that exists but is wrong.
